**Table 10.1** (generated by program ch10.2.sas in the supplemental material) presents the values of power of the Wald test and total expected treatment failures for several scenarios of a trial with $n=100$ patients. Six rules are compared: 1:1 allocation, 2:1 allocation, and four optimal allocation rules: (1)–(4). In terms of power, the four optimal allocation rules are almost identical to 1:1 allocation; however, 2:1 allocation has 1% to 8% lower power than the other rules. The RSIHR (2), score (3), and compound optimal (4) allocation result in modest but consistent reductions in the expected number of treatment failures compared to 1:1 allocation. These numbers are 1 to 3 fewer failures when the absolute difference between treatment success probabilities is 0.2 to 0.3, and it can be 3 to 6 failures when difference between success probabilities is 0.4. The 2:1 allocation yields the lowest number of failures when $p_{PE} > p_{PC}$.
